description: plx.find refuses a property the type does not declare, and carries no Portal freshness gap on a host without the Portal. operating.host cycles (Host.cycle: a GET-only BC capture of the named entity sets into a throwaway host state in {tmp}, then the projection build) on a BC-only host configuration the module writes beside that state: no Portal, mail or SharePoint configured; the capture principal and the reader granted the BC environment, the reader also the Portal relations (a MANAGER holds the Portal too). The tools are the ones the host's mcp serves over that state (Host.served_tools), called as the reader staff:manager with the clearance the Portal MANAGER role bootstraps under examples/employee_permission_policy.example.json. (b) For every served object type a plx.find filter on a property the type does not declare (the most common property name of other types) must answer unknown_property whose hint lists the type's declared properties: all of them, or the ones it names plus a (+N more) counting exactly the rest, never one name in passing (unknown_property_missed, hint_names_valid). (c) Over every type the projection holds, a filter on a declared property (present) and one that matches nothing (present and absent) must never be refused (declared_refused) and must carry no portal_api freshness gap (portal_freshness_gaps: freshness_unknown, source_unavailable, stale_source) but the source_not_configured gap (portal_not_configured_gaps >= 1: the reader holds the Portal relations, so a find that matches nothing names the Portal among its searched sources). A BC cycle that did not answer is a blocked_upstream part (blocked, never a pass); a 429/503 throttle is one part per entity set it left unread, typed error_code upstream_throttled. Every answer is validated against its frozen contract. Output is counts, booleans, codes and states only; never a value, number, name, identifier or citation.
notes: Live-unverified until the live check records a result. Module tests: injected-transport (tests/test_live_employee_tools.py runs this spec's own argv over the BC fake of integrations/tests/test_bc_capture.py and checks it with live_verify.check_expectations; only the live size floors may miss there, and each check is also run against a reproduction of the defect it guards, which it must fail). (c) lives here because it is a plx.find answer on the same host. The capture (purchase orders with their lines, vendors, items) gets 60% of the budget and may stop at it: what it holds is projected and only gives the declared-property finds types to run over. With BC down the unknown_property half still runs (blocked, measured in part).
